title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & Templates, API Examples — Docs Site Ops and Top Support Issues (Canonical Fixes)
author: Elena Park
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook documents the canonical SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, and the docs-site operating procedures used by the Developer Experience (DevEx) team. It also records the most common support issues we see for SDKs and quickstarts, the root causes, and the canonical fixes we apply to prevent recurrence.

Audience:
- SDK authors and maintainers
- DevEx documentation owners
- Support engineers who triage developer-facing issues
- Product/engineering owners publishing API changes

Scope:
This page covers: templates (SDK guide, Quickstart, API example), the publication and review workflow for docs-site changes, labeling/versioning conventions, and a prioritized list of top support issues with canonical fixes and preventative documentation changes.

Ownership and SLAs
- Primary owner: DevEx Documentation (eng-developer-experience)
- Secondary owners: SDK teams (runtime-sdk, cli-sdk), Support (customer-success)
- Review SLA: 3 business days for minor updates, 7 business days for major changes (breaking API/SDK changes)
- Emergency patch SLA: 24 hours for docs that fix security or production-breaker mistakes

Templates (canonical locations)
Use these templates for all new or updated developer docs. Keep a single source-of-truth in the repo referenced by examples below.

| Template | Canonical path | Owner | Purpose |
|---|---:|---|---|
| SDK Guide (Python & Node) | /quickstarts-and-templates/sdk-guide-template.md | devex | Reference + migration notes + examples + troubleshooting |
| Quickstart (one-page) | /quickstarts-and-templates/quickstart-template.md | devex | 5-minute starter with copy-paste code, auth, and next steps |
| API Example (endpoint-focused) | /quickstarts-and-templates/api-example-template.md | devex | Concrete request/response snippets, errors, and metrics |

SDK Guide Template (required sections)
- Title + short description (1 sentence)
- When to use this SDK (use cases)
- Install and quick import (PyPI/npm commands)
- Authentication (token rotation, env var examples)
- Basic usage examples (sync, async, streaming if supported)
- Advanced: batching, retry/backoff, pagination, streaming best practices
- Observability hooks (how to emit traces/metrics)
- Troubleshooting + common errors (include exact error text and remediation)
- Versioning and migration notes (breaking changes, upgrade path)
- Tests & CI snippet (example GitHub Actions job or test matrix)

Quickstart Template (required elements)
1) One-line summary
2) Quick prerequisites (API key, region)
3) Copy-paste install + minimal example (<= 12 lines)
4) What you should see (expected output)
5) Next steps and links to full SDK guide and API reference
6) TL;DR troubleshooting tips

API Example Template (required elements)
- Endpoint description and intent
- Minimal request & response (JSON)
- Common error responses + HTTP status codes
- Performance guidance (typical latency, token limits, model variants)
- Sample SDK usage for each official language (short snippet)
- Acceptance tests or curl snippets for CI validation

Docs Site Operating Procedures
Publication workflow (recommended):
1. Create a branch in docs repository with a clear branch name: docs/<area>/<short-desc> (e.g., docs/sdk/python-streaming-fix)
2. Update the appropriate template and content files. Add examples and a minimal automated test if applicable (see "Docs CI" below).
3. Open a Pull Request targeted at main with the following checklist completed in the PR description (PR checklist):
   - Short summary of change and motivation
   - Screenshots or example output for code changes
   - Link to related customer issues (if any) or internal bug ID
   - Linting passed (pre-commit)
   - Docs unit tests (curl examples or example-run validations)
   - Reviewer(s) from required teams assigned (see Ownership matrix)
4. Reviewer approves and merges. For breaking changes, ensure a canary publish and coordinate announcement via #devex-docs and support channel.

PR checklist (required labels and approvals):
- Labels required: docs, area-sdk (or area-quickstart/area-api-example), release-impact
- Approvers required: devex lead + owning SDK team (for code examples) + security if auth changes
- If change affects examples used in quickstarts in the public site, add label: public-breaking and notify growth and marketing teams 2 business days before merge.

Docs CI (what to include):
- Lint: markdownlint, link-checker against staging environment
- Example validation: Run Node and Python snippets in a containerized job that executes example commands and verifies expected output (exit code and sample output match)
- Spelling & grammar: run a grammar check job for user-facing text
- Publish test: preview site build step that uploads to a staging bucket and creates a review URL

Versioning & Tagging Conventions
- Examples and quickstarts must declare the SDK version and runtime: e.g., "SDK: @redwood/sdk@1.5.0 (python 3.10)"
- When publishing a breaking API change, create a docs-release note with semver tag and migration steps
- Keep a short changelog at the top of long guides (last 3 changes)

Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes (priority order)
1) Auth failures in copy-paste quickstarts
   - Symptom: Users copy sample code, insert token, get 401 with message: "invalid_api_key"
   - Root cause: Quickstart examples show inline token placeholder without guidance on env vars or KMS usage; many users paste tokens with quotes/newlines or obsolete token scopes
   - Canonical fix: Update quickstart to use ENV_VAR example and add two commands showing how to set env var for macOS/Linux and Windows. Add a troubleshooting entry that lists the exact error output and steps to verify token scopes via CLI: "redwood auth audit --token "$TOKEN""
   - Docs change required: Quickstart template updated and add a pre-flight check snippet at top of quickstarts.

2) Streaming responses break in Node streaming helper
   - Symptom: Client receives incomplete JSON when streaming structured outputs; SDK helper fails to reassemble chunks for JSONL/NDJSON
   - Root cause: Example used naive line-splitting logic that assumes newline-delimited JSON; recent runtime switched to chunked JSON tokens without final newline
   - Canonical fix: Replace helper with robust incremental JSON parser (provide examples for both Node and Python). Update SDK guide streaming section with recommended buffer/timeout settings and sample backpressure handling.
   - Docs change required: Add streaming robustness checklist and sample integration test that runs against staging runtime.

3) Embeddings shape/size mismatch on batching
   - Symptom: Customers see HTTP 400 with "invalid input shape" when sending batched embedding requests from the Python client
   - Root cause: Quickstarts show per-item string examples; batch API expects list[list[float]] or explicit flattening depending on SDK version. SDK behavior changed between 1.2.x and 1.4.x without a clear migration note in docs.
   - Canonical fix: Add explicit batch examples for the most common languages, include a compatibility table mapping SDK versions to expected payload shape, and add a validation helper that normalizes inputs.
   - Docs change required: Update SDK guide migration notes and the API example template to include both single-item and batch examples.

4) Incorrect rate-limit handling in examples
   - Symptom: Examples show naive retries causing spikes and 429 loops in production
   - Root cause: Example retry logic retries on all 5xx/429 without jitter or exponential backoff and lacks idempotency guidance for non-idempotent endpoints
   - Canonical fix: Provide a standard retry helper with exponential backoff + jitter and explicit guidance on which endpoints are idempotent. Include sample headers to inspect rate-limit quotas (x-rate-limit-remaining).
   - Docs change required: Update all SDK examples with the retry helper and add a checklist item for rate-limit awareness in quickstarts.

Canonical Fix Deployment Checklist (for each fix):
1. Create/update template + example in docs repo
2. Add automated example validation to Docs CI
3. Publish patch and link to support ticket(s) in PR description
4. Notify Support + #devex-docs channel with summary and example commands
5. Monitor support queue for 72 hours and reopen if recurring reports occur

Example fixes (snippets)
- Env var preflight (bash):
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY="<your-token>"
  # Verify token in CLI
  redwood auth audit --token "$REDWOOD_API_KEY"

- Node streaming helper (recommended pseudocode):
  // Accumulate chunks, attempt JSON.parse only when braces/balances indicate full object
  let buffer = ''
  onChunk(c) { buffer += c; if (looksLikeCompleteJson(buffer)) { processJSON(buffer); buffer = ''; } }

Ownership matrix (high level)
- devex-docs: Doc templates, CI, linting, publishing pipeline
- sdk-runtime-<lang>: SDK code samples and language-specific helpers
- support: triage, customer comms, validate user repros
- security: approve auth-related copy and KMS examples

Reporting and metrics
- Track the following metrics to measure docs health:
  - Time-to-first-response for doc-related support tickets
  - % of support tickets resolved by referencing docs (self-serve rate)
  - Docs CI example validation pass rate
  - Number of doc rollbacks due to errors

Appendix: Helpful links & references
- DevEx doc templates repo: github.com/redwood-inference/devex-doc-templates (canonical)
- Docs CI runbook: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/docs-site/docs-ci-runbook
- Support escalation playbook: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/escalation-playbook

Contact & escalation
- For doc publish failures or urgent customer-facing errors: ping #devex-docs and #support-urgent and file an internal incident in PagerDuty with service: docs-site
- Non-urgent changes: create a PR and assign devex lead for review

Notes
- Keep examples minimal and copy-paste safe. Avoid printing secrets, and prefer environment variables or CLI auth flows in examples.
- When in doubt, add an automated example validation job to Docs CI instead of relying on manual QA.

End of document.
